theme: A model church; Paul’s care; the apostle’s heart
readingInstruction: Read 1 Thessalonians 1:1-3:13. This is probably Paul’s earliest letter. Read it as a warm letter from a spiritual father to young believers. Notice the model they set, the way Paul describes his ministry, and the way he longs to see them.
settingTheScene: Paul planted the church in Thessalonica, the capital of Macedonia, on his second journey (Acts 17:1-9). He stayed only a few weeks before being driven out by a mob. Anxious about the young believers, he sent Timothy back; when Timothy returned with good news, Paul wrote this letter from Corinth around AD 50. It is full of encouragement, with gratitude, defense of his ministry against slander, and comfort. The Thessalonians were facing persecution and questions about those who had died.
observation: “Remembering before our God and Father your work of faith and labor of love and steadfastness of hope in our Lord Jesus Christ” (1:3).
“Because our gospel came to you not only in word, but also in power and in the Holy Spirit and with full conviction” (1:5).
“How you turned to God from idols to serve the living and true God, and to wait for his Son from heaven” (1:9-10).
“But we were gentle among you, like a nursing mother taking care of her own children” (2:7).
“We were ready to share with you not only the gospel of God but also our own selves” (2:8).
“You accepted it not as the word of men but as what it really is, the word of God, which is at work in you believers” (2:13).
“For now we live, if you are standing fast in the Lord” (3:8).
“And may the Lord make you increase and abound in love for one another and for all” (3:12).
interpretation:
The letter opens with thanksgiving. Paul remembers their “work of faith and labor of love and steadfastness of hope,” the great triad of faith, love, and hope. He knows God chose them because the gospel came “not only in word, but also in power and in the Holy Spirit and with full conviction.” They became imitators of Paul and the Lord, receiving the word in much affliction with the joy of the Holy Spirit, and became an example to all the believers in Macedonia and Achaia. The word of the Lord sounded forth from them. Everyone reports how they “turned to God from idols to serve the living and true God, and to wait for his Son from heaven, whom he raised from the dead, Jesus who delivers us from the wrath to come.” A model church: converted, serving, and waiting.

In chapter 2, Paul describes his ministry. The accusations probably were that he was a charlatan who preached for money or praise. He replies with the facts: they were bold to speak the gospel in spite of suffering at Philippi. They did not speak with error or impure motives or deceit. They were not trying to please men but God who tests the heart. They did not use flattery or greed or seek glory. “But we were gentle among you, like a nursing mother taking care of her own children.” Then, as a father, “exhorting each one of you and encouraging you and charging you to walk in a manner worthy of God, who calls you into his own kingdom and glory.” Paul’s ministry combines maternal tenderness and paternal firmness. They worked night and day so as not to burden anyone.

“And we also thank God constantly for this, that when you received the word of God, which you heard from us, you accepted it not as the word of men but as what it really is, the word of God, which is at work in you believers.” This is a key statement about preaching: faithful preaching of Scripture is the word of God. The Thessalonians suffered from their own countrymen, as the churches in Judea did from the Jews. Paul longed to see them and was hindered by Satan. “For what is our hope or joy or crown of boasting before our Lord Jesus at his coming? Is it not you?”

In chapter 3, Paul explains that he sent Timothy to strengthen them in their faith, lest they be shaken by afflictions. When Timothy returned with news of their faith and love, Paul was comforted. “For now we live, if you are standing fast in the Lord.” The prayer: “Now may our God and Father himself, and our Lord Jesus, direct our way to you, and may the Lord make you increase and abound in love for one another and for all, as we do for you, so that he may establish your hearts blameless in holiness before our God and Father, at the coming of our Lord Jesus with all his saints.” Ministry is love expressed in prayer and labor.
connection: Acts 17:1-15 tells of the Thessalonian mission. Philippians 4:15-16 mentions their gifts. 2 Corinthians 11:9 records provision from Macedonia. 1 Corinthians 13:13 pairs faith, hope, and love. Hebrews 4:12 speaks of the word of God living and active. 2 Timothy 3:16-17 teaches that all Scripture is God-breathed. Matthew 24:13 and John 15:18-20 speak of enduring persecution. Romans 8:35-39 assures of Christ’s love in suffering. Colossians 1:3-8 reflects similar thanksgiving.
application:
Thank someone who led you to Christ or taught you in the faith. Tell them.

Ask whether you are a model for others, in how you turned to God, serve, and wait.

Receive Scripture today as the word of God, which is at work in you.
prayerPrompts: Thank God for people who work in faith, labor in love, and endure in hope.
Ask him to help you be that kind of person.
Thank him for those who showed you how.
